title: What runs short on Everest?
hook: Climbers on Everest gasp for oxygen. What has actually changed about the air up there?

knows: that air gets thinner higher up
that pressure is how hard a gas pushes
doesNotKnow: that each gas in a mix pushes its share of the total pressure (its partial pressure)
that oxygen's share stays about 21% at altitude while its pressure falls

misconception: At altitude the air holds a lower percentage of oxygen.
objective: The learner can explain that on Everest's summit air is still about 21% oxygen, but the total pressure is about 31 kPa, so oxygen pushes only about 6.6 kPa against about 21 kPa at sea level: each breath holds about a third as much oxygen.

claims.text: Dry air is about 21% oxygen, and this share stays the same up to well above Everest's height; on the summit oxygen is still about 21% of the air.
claims.source: O2 mole fraction 0.2095 in dry air (US Standard Atmosphere 1976, table 3); the atmosphere is well mixed below about 80-100 km (homosphere). Demo.tsx O2 = 0.2095.

claims.text: In a standard-atmosphere model, air pressure on Everest's summit (8,849 m) is about 31 kPa, against about 101 kPa at sea level.
claims.source: ISA troposphere p = 101.325 × (1 − 2.25577e-5 h)^5.25588 kPa (ICAO Doc 7488); at h = 8849 m p = 31.44 kPa (node; Demo.tsx press). Summit height 8,848.86 m (China-Nepal survey, 2020).

claims.text: Each gas in a mixture pushes its share of the total pressure: oxygen's pressure is its fraction times the total (kPa, kilopascals, is a unit of pressure).
claims.source: Dalton's law of partial pressures (Atkins, Physical Chemistry, ch. 1).

claims.text: On the summit oxygen pushes about 6.6 kPa, against about 21.2 kPa at sea level, so each breath holds about a third as much oxygen.
claims.source: 0.2095 × 31.44 = 6.59 kPa; 0.2095 × 101.325 = 21.23 kPa; ratio 0.31 (node; Demo.tsx SUMMIT_O2). 'A third as much' per breath of the same volume at the same temperature (ideal gas).

claims.text: Measured summit pressure is a little higher than the model, about 34 kPa.
claims.source: West et al. 1983, J Appl Physiol 55: 678-687, barometric pressure 253 mmHg (33.7 kPa) on the summit; West 1996/2006 on why Everest pressure exceeds the standard atmosphere (latitude, season).

claims.text: The stage box is a toy: each dot stands for 0.5 kPa of air pressure, rounded to whole dots.
claims.source: Demo.tsx PER_DOT = 0.5: 203 dots at sea level, 63 at the summit; oxygen dots round(0.2095 × p / 0.5): 42 and 13. Readouts show the unrounded kPa.

claims.text: (Recall) Airliner cabins are kept at about 75 kPa.
claims.source: 14 CFR 25.841: cabin pressure altitude not above 8,000 ft (2,438 m) in normal operation; ISA at 2,438 m = 75.3 kPa.

recall.question: A plane cabin is kept at about 75 kPa. Compared with sea level, the cabin air's oxygen percentage is…
options: the same, about 21%, but its pressure is lower
recall.why: Thinning the air does not change the mix. Oxygen stays about 21%; its pressure is 21% of the lower total.
